tool.title: Judge a tree and record the verdict by digest
tool.description: Run the layer PR-check gates and tests on a composed tree (head) and on its base, or reuse a stored verdict whose digest is the base tree's, compare them with the layer-pr-checks compare scripts, and write a verdict record: {treeDigest, runner {kind agent|github-actions|local, id}, startedAt, finishedAt, gates [{name, exit, seconds, skipped?}], tests {total, failed, new}, verdict green|red|unknown}. With a token it publishes the verdict as the commit status `judge-tree`; `check` answers whether any runner judged a digest green; `sample` re-runs a seeded few gates of a record.

inputs.name: lock
inputs.description: The index.lock.json whose fixity digests name every instance but the caller.

inputs.name: caller
inputs.description: The caller as owner/name (or its lock instance): the entry replaced by its PR tree. Every runner must name it the same way.

inputs.name: caller-dir
inputs.description: The caller's git checkout; its HEAD^{tree} (or --sha's) is the PR tree.

inputs.name: sha
inputs.description: The head commit: whose tree is read from --caller-dir, and where the status is published.

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: The mounted index with the caller swapped in, where run-gates.py runs.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: The own instance(s) run-gates.py judges; repeatable.

inputs.name: base-verdict
inputs.description: A stored verdict record standing in for the base run; refused unless its treeDigest is the base tree's (--base-tree).

inputs.name: base-root
inputs.description: A mounted base tree to run the gates on instead.

inputs.name: test-path
inputs.description: What `bun test` runs on each side; none means no tests.

inputs.name: publish
inputs.description: Post the commit status `judge-tree` when GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN is set; without one, the record file is the verdict.

outputs.name: record
outputs.description: The verdict record, `<records-dir>/<treeDigest>.json` unless --out names it; valid against the tools layer's `schemas/verdict-record.schema.json`. Three exit codes: 0 green, 1 red, 2 COULD NOT DETERMINE (no judging scripts, a stored base verdict for another tree, a compare script that crashed, or no gate ran). 2 is never green, and neither is a verdict for another digest.

selection.when: When a PR's tree must be judged and any runner can do it: an agent before pushing, a developer locally, or CI. Then `verdict-check.yml` passes the PR on the published verdict instead of re-running ~300 gates per side.
selection.limits: The digest trusts the lock's fixity digests for every instance but the caller, so a run that takes lower layers at main instead of the lock judges a tree the digest does not name. A verdict answers only for its exact digest: a change to the judging scripts is a new digest and needs a new verdict.
selection.cost: That of layer-pr-checks for one side, or two when no stored base verdict exists: gates dominate (minutes to tens of minutes). `digest` and `check` are one hash and at most one HTTP request.

remedies.none: Publishing and `check` against statuses need the API; without it the record file is the verdict and `check --records-dir` reads records instead.

$comment.comment:
── Judge a tree once, on any runner, and say so by digest ─────────────

Owner, 2026-10-16: "github should be one Tool of
several". `gates` RUNS the checks in one checkout; this judges a whole
composed TREE head-against-base and leaves a verdict record anyone can
find again by the tree's digest. The digest is the index lock's fixity
digests (each instance's declaration sha256 and directory treeDigests,
as mount-from-lock checks them), the caller's entry replaced by its PR
tree (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`), and the judging-scripts version. Same
bytes, same digest, whichever runner computed it: an agent container, a
local machine, or GitHub Actions. GitHub is where a verdict is PUBLISHED
(the commit status `judge-tree`), not where it must be reached.

The implementation is the tools layer's `scripts/judge-tree.ts`; the
record's shape is its `schemas/verdict-record.schema.json`
(`cat-harness-verdict-record/v1`).
